question: The picked choice is now a tinted glass chip that stretches across as it moves. Is this the effect you meant?
context: Built on 2026-09-30: our drawn segmented control is back everywhere, with the picked choice as a Liquid Glass chip tinted with the accent. Tinted glass alone washed out in light (a white word read 1.6:1 on it), so the accent is laid over the glass. Filmed at 120 fps in the title bar, a panel row and the history bar: it stretches across and never leaves the rail.

options.label: Yes, keep it
options.summary: Every row of choices keeps our grey rail with the accent-tinted glass chip, white word on it, stretching across in about a third of a second.
pros: Every word measured at 4.5:1 or better on the real window, light and dark
Same control and same motion in the title bar, the panel and the history bar
cons: The accent covers most of the glass, so the chip reads more as a coloured pill with a glass rim than as clear glass
options.mitigation: The glass still shows at the rim and a little through; a later pass can tune how much once you have lived with it.

options.label: More glass, dark word
options.summary: The chip becomes mostly glass with only a light accent tint, and the picked word turns dark instead of white so it stays readable.
pros: Looks more like clear Liquid Glass
A dark word reads well on a pale chip
cons: No longer white on the accent, which is what you asked for
The pick stands out less from the rail at a glance
options.mitigation: The chip keeps a stronger accent rim so the pick is still easy to find.

options.label: Keep it, slower stretch
options.summary: Same look, but the chip takes about half a second to travel so the stretch is easier to see.
pros: The liquid stretch is more visible
cons: A slower control can feel sluggish when clicking quickly
options.mitigation: A quick second click still retargets the chip from wherever it is.
